# Blender models of construction projects

Dimensionally accurate, provenance-tracked 3D models of restoration and defect-repair work in occupied
multifamily buildings, built headless in Blender from construction drawings, details, specs and site photos.
Accuracy first, realism second: every dimension traces to a source or is labeled assumed, automated checks
must pass, and the renders get looked at. Agents: **[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)**. How models are made: **[docs/METHOD.md](docs/METHOD.md)** ·
step-by-step commands: **[docs/RUNBOOK.md](docs/RUNBOOK.md)**.

## Quickstart

```bash
uv sync                                   # Python 3.11 + locked bpy 5.0.1, PyMuPDF, OpenCV (one environment)
uv run bm doctor                          # what this machine can run, and the fix for each gap
uvx pre-commit install                    # once per clone: blocks oversized or unsourced commits
uv run bm list                            # sites, specs, products
uv run bm new <site> --type detail        # start a project from templates/project/
uv run bm build <site>                    # build + verify every spec of a site (or <site>/<spec>)
uv run bm check                           # provenance, metadata, large files, links, tests
```

Linux needs the X11 libraries bpy links against:
`sudo apt-get install libx11-6 libxrender1 libxfixes3 libxi6 libxext6 libxkbcommon0 libsm6 libice6 libgl1`.
Always run Python through uv (`uv run python …`, `uv run bm …`). Node pieces (browser viewers, Playwright
films) use npm inside their product folder.

## Layout

```
projects/<site>/
  project.yaml               name, address, building type, scope, release tag prefix
  sources/manifest.json      inventory of drawings and photos (the files themselves stay out of git)
  specs/*.yaml               spec-driven models: detail | house | room | element  → `bm build`
  takeoff/                   extracted plan data the specs read
  products/<name>/           bespoke pipelines (films, viewers, bid models) + product.yaml steps → `bm run`
  deliverables/<name>/       what gets handed over: READMEs, previews; large files via Releases
src/bmodels/                 the shared toolkit and the `bm` CLI
templates/project/           what `bm new` copies
assets/                      shared CC0 assets (HDRIs)
render/                      saved-scene shot catalog for the render-scenes workflow
docs/                        METHOD.md, RUNBOOK.md
```

## Sites

| Site | Name | Specs | Products |
|---|---|---|---|
| [field-parapet](projects/field-parapet/) | Field parapet (site photo P1) | field-parapet-existing, field-parapet-proposed | — |
| [highland](projects/highland/) | 200 W. Highland condominiums | — | exterior, installation, repipe, walkthrough, water |
| [meydenbauer-b](projects/meydenbauer-b/) | 101 Meydenbauer, Building B | — | underslab |
| [qp-cottage-a](projects/qp-cottage-a/) | Quail Park of Lynnwood — Cottage Duplex A | qp-cottage-a, qp-rake-ah700-12 | — |
| [room-living-kitchen](projects/room-living-kitchen/) | Living room / kitchen (occupied apartment) | room-living-kitchen | — |
| [sample](projects/sample/) | SAMPLE — pipeline fixture (not a real project) | sample-bay | — |

Regenerate with `uv run bm list --markdown`. Highlights: Highland
[archviz walkthrough](projects/highland/deliverables/archviz/README.md),
[installation film](projects/highland/deliverables/installation/README.md),
[cinema shot list](projects/highland/products/walkthrough/CINEMA.md) (film not published);
Meydenbauer [bid model, realism views and 4D films](projects/meydenbauer-b/deliverables/underslab/README.md).

## Commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `bm doctor [--json]` · `bm list [--json \| --markdown]` | environment gaps with fixes · full inventory (spec kinds, product steps, deliverables) |
| `bm new <site>` · `bm add-product <site>/<name>` | scaffold a site · a product with a CI `check` step |
| `bm build [path \| site \| site/spec] [--realistic] [--changed BASE]` | build, verify and render specs → `build/<site>/<spec>/` |
| `bm run <site>/<product> [<step> [args]]` | run a step declared in `product.yaml` (no step: list them) |
| `bm check [--staged \| --base REF]` · `bm check-products` | repo checks · every product's `check` step |
| `bm publish <site>/<product> <files…>` · `bm assets pull\|verify <manifest>` | large outputs to/from GitHub Releases |
| `bm calibrate`, `extract`, `overlay`, `detail-overlay` | drawing intake (see the runbook) |
| `bm render`, `render-plan`, `animate-house`, `animate-sequence`, `room`, `skp`, `usdz`, `audit-blends` | renders, sequences, exports, scene audit |

## Large files

New files over 1 MB (MP4, .blend, ZIP, EXR, GLB, big GIF/HTML) go to **GitHub Releases**, not git:
`uv run bm publish <site>/<product> <files…>` uploads them, records sha256 in the product's
`release-assets.json`, keeps the local copies out of git and prints README links; `uv run bm assets pull
<manifest>` restores them. `bm check` (pre-commit and CI) rejects new oversized files. Files already in Git LFS
stay there and may be updated; nothing new goes to LFS.

## CI

| Workflow | When | What |
|---|---|---|
| `build-models` | specs, takeoff, products, `src/`, lock change | `bm build --changed` (every spec when code or the lock changes) and `bm check-products` (changed products and their `depends_on` dependents); reports in the job summary, `build/` as artifact |
| `checks` | every PR and push to main | `bm check --base …` (provenance, metadata, large files, links, tests) and `bm audit-blends` |
| `render-scenes` | `render/`, renderer or project changes | render each shot in `render/scenes.json` on CPU and validate the pixels |
| `highland-*` | manual | Highland native film, archviz review and preview renders |

Every workflow sets up through `.github/actions/setup-blender-env` (apt libraries, setup-uv cached on
`uv.lock`, `uv sync --frozen`). Pushes from a local clone can change workflow files; cloud agent tokens
without the `workflow` scope cannot.
# Method

How every model in this repo is made, whatever the site or model type. Operator commands step by step:
[RUNBOOK.md](RUNBOOK.md). Repo layout and tools: [../README.md](../README.md).

Purpose: build dimensionally accurate, realistic 3D models of restoration and defect-repair projects (occupied multifamily) from construction drawings, details, specs, and site photos, using Blender driven by Python. Accuracy first, realism second. A model is finished only when every dimension traces to a source or is labeled as assumed, the automated checks pass, and the renders have been looked at.

## Pipeline (always in this order)

1. **Intake.** Inventory every source: sheet number, detail number, revision/date, scale, photo IDs. Read drawings at full resolution (rasterize PDFs with `pdftoppm -r 200+`; crop into details). Note scale bars and "NTS" details.
2. **Takeoff.** Extract every dimension, member size, spacing, elevation, and count into the model spec. Use actual lumber sizes (2x10 = 1½ × 9¼), not nominal. Never scale an NTS detail. Never infer a dimension from a partial drawing and call it documented.
3. **Model spec** (`projects/<site>/specs/<area>.yaml`; start a site with `uv run bm new <site>`). The spec is the single source of truth; geometry is never hand-edited in Blender without the spec changing too. Every element carries:
   - `status: confirmed` — dimension shown on a document (`source` required)
   - `status: provisional` — derived: scaled from a drawing with a scale bar, or measured from a photo against a known reference (`source` required; note the reference and expected tolerance)
   - `status: assumed` — not in any document (`basis` required, e.g. "code-minimum", "typical", "massing only")
   - Document-driven `checks`: counts, overall extents, clear gaps, spacing, elevations — each with its `source`.
4. **Build.** `uv run bm build <site>[/<spec>] [--realistic]` (bpy, headless). One collection per trade; trades stay separate. Inches in the spec; Blender stores meters, displays imperial.
5. **Verify.** The builder fails (exit 1) on: missing source/basis, count or extent mismatch, gap mismatch, or a blank render. Then look at the review renders myself — plan, front, side, iso — colored by provenance (green confirmed, yellow provisional, orange assumed). Where a drawing elevation exists, compare the ortho render against it at the same scale. "Checks passed" and "looked right" are both required; report which were done.
6. **Realism pass** (only after geometry is verified). PBR materials by real product where known; realistic lighting via Cycles. Realism never changes geometry.
7. **Quantities.** Every house build writes `<name>_takeoff.xlsx` (src/bmodels/qto.py): openings schedule, siding + gable panel net of openings by elevation, casing and corner-board LF, roof area by pitch, squares (waste is a yellow input), ridge/hip/valley/eave/rake LF, and an Elements sheet of stable IDs for trackers. Measured values are blue inputs with method + status; everything derived is a live formula. Reconcile against any documented quantity (Cottage A: plan roof area 3,935.7 vs 3,935 sf on AH202).
8. **Deliver.** `.blend` (editable), `.glb` (phone/web viewing, carries element metadata), review renders, `report.md`. List every assumed element in the handoff.

## Plan-set method (proven on QP Cottage A, 2026-09-27)

- **Calibrate every sheet from its own dimension strings** before measuring anything: find the tick marks of a long dimension and compute pt/ft (AH201: 39'-0" ticks 702 pt apart = 18.0 pt/ft = true 1/4"). Never trust the title-block scale alone.
- **Rasterize at an exact scale** (2 px/in plans, 1–2 px/in elevations). Walls drawn as hollow outlines are found as thin enclosed white cores (half-width 2.5–7.5 px); window glazing splits the band into strips under 2.3 px half-width.
- **Every extracted opening must appear on an elevation** or it is rejected (tubs, showers, garage-door lines and revision clouds all produce false openings). Record rejected candidates in the spec.
- **Revision clouds and tags break linework** — look for missing wall where a cloud crosses, trace it manually, and add it as an `extra_walls` entry with its reason.
- **Mirror-image units:** extract the cleaner half and mirror, but first measure the match (Cottage A: 94% of walls within 1½").
- **Roofs:** union of convex hip/gable pieces taken from the eave outline on the roof plan; verify predicted ridge/hip positions against the drawn ones and ridge heights against elevations.
- **Walls are built boolean-free** (rectangle decomposition, openings cut by box splitting). Roof unions use Blender's **Manifold** boolean solver — the Exact solver fails on the coplanar faces that roofs inevitably have.
- **Overlay check:** `src/bmodels/overlay.py` renders the model orthographically at the drawing's scale and overlays it on the elevation; report the edge-agreement % and look at the image.

## Model types

- **detail** — one construction section (rake, eave, balcony edge, window head) as callout-sized components swept along a short path; 1/16" intent. `src/bmodels/detail.py`.
- **house** — plan-extracted shell (walls, openings, roof) + quantity takeoff. `src/bmodels/house.py`, `src/bmodels/qto.py`.
- **room** — interior shell + furniture + lighting from a photo or sketch (`projects/<site>/specs/room-*.yaml`, `src/bmodels/room.py`). Photo-only, so nothing can be `confirmed`: every group is `provisional` (visible, sized from a reference) or `assumed`. Checks are internal consistency (body corners match the spec, clearances, footprints don't overlap), not accuracy to the real room. `src/bmodels/build.py` hands room specs to `room.py` (checks + review renders only, so CI needs no workflow change). Run `uv run bm room projects/room-living-kitchen/specs/room-living-kitchen.yaml [--only review_iso,photomatch_night] [--no-render]`; the full render set is ~25 min on 4 CPU cores.
- **element / building** — not built yet: parametric components (balcony, stair) and multi-level buildings with repeated units.
All types share: provenance on every element, failing checks, CI rebuild.

## Accuracy rules

- Never present an assumed or provisional element as documented. Review renders always show provenance colors; realistic renders shared outside the team must carry a note if any assumed elements are visible.
- Photos: state the reference object used for scale (brick course, CMU, door, siding exposure, known member size), the camera angle limits, and the resulting tolerance. Photo-only geometry is at best `provisional`.
- Conflicts between sources (drawing vs. photo vs. spec): model per the governing document, flag the conflict in the report — don't average or silently pick.
- Existing-conditions models (defect repair) and proposed-repair models are separate scenes or separate specs. Don't merge them.
- Models are illustrative/coordination tools, not contract documents. Any render used in a scope, PCO, or resident notice gets that label.

### Spec record fields (enforced by `bm check` and `bm build`)

- `basis_of_record` (required): `documents` (what the model is built from), `kind` (`design_intent`,
  `as_built`, `field_photo`, `field_survey`, `mixed`, `unknown`), `field_verified` (`verified`, `partial`,
  `not_verified`, `unknown`), optional `note`. It goes at the top of every report and on every render.
- `conflicts` (optional): `{topic, note, modeled_per: <source id>, sources: [...]}`, one per source
  conflict. `modeled_per` must name the governing source. Listed under "Source conflicts" in the report.
- `assumptions` (optional): `{id, basis}` for assumed parameters not tied to one element.
- `review` (optional): `{date, by, views: [...], overlays: [{view, verdict: pass|fail|n/a, edge_pct, note}]}`.
  Add it only after you have looked at the renders. Until then the report says "Visual review: NOT RECORDED".
- Every render gets a strip appended below the image (never over the geometry): "ILLUSTRATIVE: coordination
  model, not a contract document", the record kind, field-verification status and provenance counts.

## Occupied-building use cases

Resident notices (what's happening at their unit), access and sequencing diagrams, protection/staging/egress layouts, and PCO backup showing concealed conditions. For these, include the relevant occupied-building elements (egress paths, protection, staging area, work zone) as their own collection, marked by source like everything else.

## Environment facts (verified 2026-09-27)

- `uv sync` installs Python 3.11 and the locked `bpy==5.0.1` (see `pyproject.toml`); always run Python as `uv run python …`; build + checks for a small spec run in seconds.
- Headless has no GPU: **Workbench and EEVEE render blank frames** — use Cycles on CPU only. Cameras need explicit rotation (track-to constraints are not evaluated before headless renders).
- Exports confirmed working: .blend, .glb, .obj, .stl, .fbx, .usdz. SVG import add-on present. IFC (Bonsai) not installed — unverified.
- Cycles realistic render: ~2 min for 4 review views + 1 realistic view at 1600×1200 on 2 CPU cores. EEVEE took 45 s for a trivial scene and still returned blank.

## Working style

Ask once, batched, only for what can't be read from the documents (e.g. a missing detail, which revision governs). Otherwise take the next step and mark assumptions. Don't claim a model is accurate beyond what its sources support.

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- build
def changed_specs(base):
    try:
        files = checks._git("diff", "--name-only", f"{base}...HEAD")
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
        files = checks._git("diff", "--name-only", base, "HEAD")
    files = [f for f in files if f]
    if any(f.startswith(REBUILD_ALL) for f in files):
        return project.all_specs()
    picked = set()
    for s in project.sites():
        d = str(rel(s.dir)) + "/"
        # specs read takeoff/sources data from anywhere in the site except products and deliverables
        if any(f.startswith(d) and not f.startswith((d + "products/", d + "deliverables/")) for f in files):
            picked.update(s.specs)
    picked.update(ROOT / f for f in files if f.startswith("specs/") and f.endswith(".yaml") and (ROOT / f).exists())
    return sorted(picked)


def cmd_build(a):
    specs = changed_specs(a.changed) if a.changed else project.resolve_specs(a.targets)
    if not specs:
        print("No specs to build.")
        return 0
    flags = (["--realistic"] if a.realistic else []) + (["--no-render"] if a.no_render else [])
    summary = os.environ.get("GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY")
    failed = []
    for sp in specs:
        out = project.build_dir(sp)
        gh = bool(os.environ.get("GITHUB_ACTIONS"))
        print(f"::group::{rel(sp)}" if gh else f"== {rel(sp)} -> {rel(out)}/{sp.stem}/", flush=True)
        code = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "bmodels.build", str(sp), "--out", str(out), *flags], check=False).returncode
        if gh:
            print("::endgroup::")
        if code:
            failed.append(rel(sp))
        report = out / sp.stem / "report.md"
        if summary and report.exists():
            with open(summary, "a") as f:
                f.write(report.read_text() + "\n")
    print(f"\n{len(specs) - len(failed)}/{len(specs)} specs passed" + (f"; failed: {', '.join(map(str, failed))}" if failed else ""))
    if failed:
        print(DOCTOR_HINT)
    return 1 if failed else 0

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

@AGENTS.md

## Architecture (the parts that span files)

- **`bm` CLI** (`src/bmodels/cli.py`, entry point `bm = bmodels.cli:main`). Most subcommands shell out to
  `python -m bmodels.<module>` (e.g. `bm build` runs `python -m bmodels.build <spec> --out build/<site>/`
  once per spec). Pass-through tools (`render`, `room`, `skp`, `usdz`, `audit-blends`, …) map 1:1 to modules.
- **Spec pipeline.** `spec.py` loads a spec and checks its provenance without bpy, so `bm check` and CI planning
  work anywhere. `build.py` (needs bpy) sends each element to a builder by `type`: `detail` → `detail.py`,
  `house` → `house.py`, plus `qto.py` for the xlsx takeoff. A spec with top-level `items` is a room spec
  and goes whole to `room.py`. Then `verify()` runs the spec's `checks` and blank-render guards are added.
  The `.blend`/`.glb`/PNGs are written and `record.py` writes `report.md`/`report.json`. Any failed check
  exits 1.
- **`bm build --changed BASE`** picks specs from the git diff. A change under `src/` or to the lock rebuilds
  every spec. A change anywhere in a site except `products/`/`deliverables/` rebuilds that site's specs.
- **`bm check`** (`checks.py`) checks specs, site/product metadata, large files (with `--staged`/`--base` only)
  and markdown links, then runs `pytest -q`.
- **`src/cie/`**: the Construction Intelligence Engine semantic kernel (claims, evidence, elements, scenarios).
  It is a second package, separate from `bmodels`, specified in `docs/CONSTRUCTION_INTELLIGENCE_SPEC.md`.
  The `tests/test_cie_*` and `tests/test_meydenbauer_*` tests exercise it.

## Tests

- `uv run pytest -q`; one test: `uv run pytest tests/test_bm.py -k <name> -q`.
- Most tests are bpy-free. Tests that need bpy skip when it can't be imported (e.g. `test_render_workflow.py`),
  so a green run on this laptop doesn't cover them; CI does.
- Lint: `uv run ruff check` (line length 120).

**What it produces:** two separate models of the building's domestic water distribution, from the P1 garage
main through the R1 Corridor 108 header to every riser and floor takeoff up to R5:

- **existing** (`risers-existing.spec.json`): the system as drawn in the October 2007 plumbing set;
- **proposed** (`risers-proposed.spec.json`): a PEX-A replacement installed alongside the live system, then cut

Each spec builds to a `.blend`, a `.glb` (with `cie_id`, `cie_status`, `cie_system`, `phase` on every object) and
four labelled review renders. Deliverables: [../../deliverables/risers](../../deliverables/risers/README.md).

**Illustrative, not a contract document.** Drawing-traced, not a survey of installed piping.

Registered in [source-manifest.json](source-manifest.json). The PDFs stay in `projects/highland/sources/`.

| RL-REVISED Highland Condos Plumbing 10-29-07, P2.01–P2.07 | Riser positions (vector markups), main and header routes (linework) | XY **provisional**, ±12 in at risers, ±18 in on runs |

| S3.8 (04-02-07) | R1 drop-slab soffit 351.21 ft (bounds the garage main) | reference only |

How the trace works:

- The plumbing sheets carry vector PDF markups that follow the sheet legend: green "continuous riser or riser
  going up", orange "riser going down", and cyan, magenta and lime for CW, HW and HWC.
- `extract.py` finds the grid bubbles on each sheet and fits them to the A2.03 dimension strings. Every P2.0x

  (x east of grid 7, y north of grid E).
- `takeoff.py` averages the boxes at each stack across floors. Stacks agree within 2–8.5 in floor to floor.
  Crops at every stack and floor are in [source-review/](source-review/) so the trace can be checked without
  the PDF.

You are a Lead Technical Artist and Blender Python (`bpy`) Automation Agent. Your objective is to transform raw Virtual Design & Construction (VDC), BIM, or CAD geometry imports inside Blender into **ultra-high-end, path-traced architectural films**. 

Raw VDC exports look like engineering diagrams because they suffer from six systemic flaws:

2. Unnatural continuous "robot spline" camera paths that clip through doors and stare into corners.

## 2. Universal Architectural & Cinematography Rules

When inspecting, modifying, or generating cameras, lights, and geometry in any scene, enforce these non-negotiable rules:

### Rule 1: Two-Point Perspective (Architectural Tilt-Shift)
* **Never tilt an architectural camera up or down** to frame a building or interior. Vertical architectural lines (walls, columns, doorframes, mullions) must remain 100% parallel to the left and right edges of the frame.
* Lock every camera's `rotation_euler.x = math.radians(90)` and `rotation_euler.y = 0.0`.
* Frame vertical height exclusively by adjusting `camera.data.shift_y` (typically `-0.05` to `+0.15`).
* Use `24mm–35mm` focal lengths (`36mm` full-frame sensor width) in **16:9 Widescreen** (`3840x2160`).

### Rule 2: Multi-Camera Linear Cuts Over Single-Spline Paths
* Never use a single continuous camera spline that twists 90 degrees inside tight corridors or ghosts through closed doors.
* Break the journey into discrete **3-to-5-second cinematic shots** (`CAM_01`, `CAM_02`, etc.) bound to Timeline Markers.
* Force **100% `LINEAR` keyframe interpolation** on all camera location/rotation f-curves so camera movement feels like a constant-velocity Steadicam or dolly track across cuts.
* Any door in the camera's path must be keyframed open (`75°–90°` swing or linear slide) prior to the camera crossing the threshold.

### Rule 3: Narrative "Compression & Release"
* Never end an architectural tour in an enclosed service space (corridors, stairwells, mechanical rooms, or elevator lobbies).
* Circulation spaces are the **Compression Phase** (controlled, warm 3500K artificial light). The final shot of the sequence must always transition into a **Release Phase**—a sunlit destination with high ceilings, natural exterior light (`2800K–4000K` low-angle sun + Sky Portals), and exterior context views.

* Never rely on high-strength `ShaderNodeEmission` materials on ceiling fixtures to light an interior—this creates fireflies and clips into flat white blocks.

    print("\n================ VDC SCENE AUDIT REPORT ================")
    print(f"File: {bpy.data.filepath or 'Unsaved File'}")
    print(f"Current Engine: {scene.render.engine} | FPS: {scene.render.fps} | Frames: {scene.frame_start}-{scene.frame_end}")

    print("\n1. COLLECTIONS:")
    for col in bpy.data.collections:

    # Compute overall scene bounding box
    meshes = [o for o in scene.objects if o.type == 'MESH' and not o.hide_render]
    if meshes:
        min_co = mathutils.Vector((1e9, 1e9, 1e9))
        max_co = mathutils.Vector((-1e9, -1e9, -1e9))
        for obj in meshes:
            for corner in obj.bound_box:

                min_co.y = min(min_co.y, world_co.y)

                max_co.x = max(max_co.x, world_co.x)

    print("\n3. CAMERAS & ANIMATED RIGS:")

    scene.cycles.glossy_bounces = 4
    scene.cycles.transmission_bounces = 8

    try:

                    noise.location = (node.location.x - 500, node.location.y - 100)

                    ramp.inputs['To Min'].default_value = max(0.05, base_r - 0.06)

                    ramp.location = (node.location.x - 280, node.location.y - 100)

                    links.new(noise.outputs['Fac'], ramp.inputs['Value'])

            elif node.type == 'EMISSION':

    # =========================================================================

# Agent Directive: Universal $20k VDC-to-Archviz Upgrade Pipeline (Blender `bpy`)

## 1. Mission & Role
You are a Lead Technical Artist and Blender Python (`bpy`) Automation Agent. Your objective is to transform raw Virtual Design & Construction (VDC), BIM, or CAD geometry imports inside Blender into **ultra-high-end, path-traced architectural films**. 

Raw VDC exports look like engineering diagrams because they suffer from six systemic flaws:
1. Clipped highlight values from standard sRGB color management.
2. Unnatural continuous "robot spline" camera paths that clip through doors and stare into corners.
3. Razor-sharp 90-degree polygon edges and flat, zero-imperfection shaders.
4. Blown-out emissive ceiling strips and visible light-source specular blobs.
5. Technical cross-sections that reveal untextured background massing.
6. Lack of narrative emotional payoff ("Compression & Release").

You must systematically eliminate all six flaws on any target `.blend` file using the protocols and automated scripts below.

---

## 2. Universal Architectural & Cinematography Rules

When inspecting, modifying, or generating cameras, lights, and geometry in any scene, enforce these non-negotiable rules:

### Rule 1: Two-Point Perspective (Architectural Tilt-Shift)
* **Never tilt an architectural camera up or down** to frame a building or interior. Vertical architectural lines (walls, columns, doorframes, mullions) must remain 100% parallel to the left and right edges of the frame.
* Lock every camera's `rotation_euler.x = math.radians(90)` and `rotation_euler.y = 0.0`.
* Frame vertical height exclusively by adjusting `camera.data.shift_y` (typically `-0.05` to `+0.15`).
* Use `24mm–35mm` focal lengths (`36mm` full-frame sensor width) in **16:9 Widescreen** (`3840x2160`).

### Rule 2: Multi-Camera Linear Cuts Over Single-Spline Paths
* Never use a single continuous camera spline that twists 90 degrees inside tight corridors or ghosts through closed doors.
* Break the journey into discrete **3-to-5-second cinematic shots** (`CAM_01`, `CAM_02`, etc.) bound to Timeline Markers.
* Force **100% `LINEAR` keyframe interpolation** on all camera location/rotation f-curves so camera movement feels like a constant-velocity Steadicam or dolly track across cuts.
* Any door in the camera's path must be keyframed open (`75°–90°` swing or linear slide) prior to the camera crossing the threshold.

### Rule 3: Narrative "Compression & Release"
* Never end an architectural tour in an enclosed service space (corridors, stairwells, mechanical rooms, or elevator lobbies).
* Circulation spaces are the **Compression Phase** (controlled, warm 3500K artificial light). The final shot of the sequence must always transition into a **Release Phase**—a sunlit destination with high ceilings, natural exterior light (`2800K–4000K` low-angle sun + Sky Portals), and exterior context views.

### Rule 4: Separate Fixture Glow from Scene Illumination
* Never rely on high-strength `ShaderNodeEmission` materials on ceiling fixtures to light an interior—this creates fireflies and clips into flat white blocks.
* Clamp visible light fixture `Emission` nodes to `Strength: 3.0–5.0` (`#FFF4E6` warm white) so the fixture reads as diffused acrylic under AgX color management.
* Place actual Blender `AREA` lights (`Spread: 85°–105°`) just below ceiling fixtures and inside coves to cast physical light falloff, and set `light_obj.visible_camera = False` and `light_obj.visible_glossy = False` so they never create artificial specular hotspots on doors, glass, or polished floors.

---

## 3. Automated Execution Protocol

When assigned to upgrade a `.blend` project, execute the following workflow in order:

1. **Phase 1 — Scene Audit:** Run `01_scene_audit.py` to map collections, bounding boxes, existing cameras, light sources, and material counts.
2. **Phase 2 — Core Engine, Shader & Light Overhaul:** Run `02_universal_vdc_upgrader.py` to configure Cycles GPU, AgX color management, global 3mm shader micro-bevels, procedural drywall/floor micro-roughness, light ray-visibility fixes, and the optical Compositor pipeline.
3. **Phase 3 — Dynamic Camera & Section Tooling:** Use the modular functions in `03_cinematic_rigs.py` to generate level tilt-shift Steadicam shots, animated Boolean cross-section reveals with glowing cut-faces, and Window Sky Portals.

## 4. Script 1: `01_scene_audit.py` (Project-Agnostic Scene Inspector)

Run this first to understand the spatial bounds and naming conventions of the target file.

```python
import bpy
import mathutils

def audit_vdc_scene():
    scene = bpy.context.scene
    print("\n================ VDC SCENE AUDIT REPORT ================")
    print(f"File: {bpy.data.filepath or 'Unsaved File'}")
    print(f"Current Engine: {scene.render.engine} | FPS: {scene.render.fps} | Frames: {scene.frame_start}-{scene.frame_end}")

    print("\n1. COLLECTIONS:")
    for col in bpy.data.collections:
        print(f"  - {col.name}: {len(col.objects)} objects")

    # Compute overall scene bounding box
    meshes = [o for o in scene.objects if o.type == 'MESH' and not o.hide_render]
    if meshes:
        min_co = mathutils.Vector((1e9, 1e9, 1e9))
        max_co = mathutils.Vector((-1e9, -1e9, -1e9))
        for obj in meshes:
            for corner in obj.bound_box:
                world_co = obj.matrix_world @ mathutils.Vector(corner)
                min_co.x = min(min_co.x, world_co.x)
                min_co.y = min(min_co.y, world_co.y)
                min_co.z = min(min_co.z, world_co.z)
                max_co.x = max(max_co.x, world_co.x)
                max_co.y = max(max_co.y, world_co.y)
                max_co.z = max(max_co.z, world_co.z)
        print(f"\n2. WORLD BOUNDS (Meters):")
        print(f"  - Min (X,Y,Z): ({min_co.x:.2f}, {min_co.y:.2f}, {min_co.z:.2f})")
        print(f"  - Max (X,Y,Z): ({max_co.x:.2f}, {max_co.y:.2f}, {max_co.z:.2f})")
        print(f"  - Total Footprint: {(max_co.x - min_co.x):.2f}m x {(max_co.y - min_co.y):.2f}m x {(max_co.z - min_co.z):.2f}m tall")

    print("\n3. CAMERAS & ANIMATED RIGS:")
    for obj in scene.objects:
        if obj.type == 'CAMERA' or (obj.animation_data and obj.animation_data.action):
            print(f"  - {obj.name} ({obj.type}) at {[round(c, 2) for c in obj.location]}")

    print(f"\n4. TOTALS: {len(meshes)} Meshes | {len(bpy.data.materials)} Materials | {len([o for o in scene.objects if o.type == 'LIGHT'])} Lights")
    print("========================================================\n")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    audit_vdc_scene()
```

## 5. Script 2: `02_universal_vdc_upgrader.py` (Engine, Shaders, Lights & Compositor)

Run this script on any BIM/VDC scene to immediately upgrade rendering, color science, edge bevels, surface micro-roughness, light behavior, and lens post-processing.

```python
import bpy
import math

def apply_universal_vdc_upgrades():
    scene = bpy.context.scene

    # =========================================================================
    # 1. RENDER ENGINE & AgX COLOR SCIENCE
    # =========================================================================
    scene.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
    scene.cycles.device = 'GPU'
    scene.render.resolution_x = 3840
    scene.render.resolution_y = 2160
    scene.render.resolution_percentage = 50  # 1080p fast preview; set 100 for final 4K

    # Sampling & Albedo/Normal-Preserving Denoiser
    scene.cycles.samples = 512
    scene.cycles.adaptive_threshold = 0.015
    scene.cycles.use_denoising = True
    scene.cycles.denoiser = 'OPENIMAGEDENOISE'
    scene.cycles.denoising_input_passes = 'RGB_ALBEDO_NORMAL'

    # Architectural Light Bounce Profile
    scene.cycles.max_bounces = 12
    scene.cycles.diffuse_bounces = 4
    scene.cycles.glossy_bounces = 4
    scene.cycles.transmission_bounces = 8
    scene.cycles.volume_bounces = 2
    scene.cycles.sample_clamp_indirect = 10.0

    # AgX High-Dynamic-Range View Transform
    try:
        scene.view_settings.view_transform = 'AgX'
        scene.view_settings.look = 'AgX - Medium High Contrast'
    except TypeError:
        scene.view_settings.view_transform = 'Filmic'
        scene.view_settings.look = 'Medium High Contrast'

    # =========================================================================
    # 2. GLOBAL PBR SHADER UPGRADER (Micro-Bevels + Roughness Breakup + Emissives)
    # =========================================================================
    for mat in bpy.data.materials:
        if not mat.use_nodes or not mat.node_tree:
            continue
        nodes = mat.node_tree.nodes
        links = mat.node_tree.links

        for node in list(nodes):
            if node.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED':
                # A. Inject 3mm Architectural Micro-Bevel into unlinked Normals
                if not node.inputs['Normal'].is_linked:
                    bevel = nodes.new(type='ShaderNodeBevel')
                    bevel.samples = 4
                    bevel.inputs['Radius'].default_value = 0.003
                    bevel.location = (node.location.x - 280, node.location.y - 320)
                    links.new(bevel.outputs['Normal'], node.inputs['Normal'])

                # B. Replace flat CG Roughness with subtle procedural micro-variation
                if not node.inputs['Roughness'].is_linked:
                    base_r = node.inputs['Roughness'].default_value
                    # Clamp unrealistic 1.0 chalky surfaces
                    if base_r > 0.85:
                        base_r = 0.60
                    
                    tex_coord = nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord')
                    tex_coord.location = (node.location.x - 700, node.location.y - 100)
                    
                    noise = nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexNoise')
                    noise.inputs['Scale'].default_value = 120.0
                    noise.inputs['Detail'].default_value = 8.0
                    noise.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = 0.6
                    noise.location = (node.location.x - 500, node.location.y - 100)
                    
                    ramp = nodes.new('ShaderNodeMapRange')
                    ramp.inputs['To Min'].default_value = max(0.05, base_r - 0.06)
                    ramp.inputs['To Max'].default_value = min(0.95, base_r + 0.06)
                    ramp.location = (node.location.x - 280, node.location.y - 100)
                    
                    links.new(tex_coord.outputs['Object'], noise.inputs['Vector'])
                    links.new(noise.outputs['Fac'], ramp.inputs['Value'])
                    links.new(ramp.outputs['Result'], node.inputs['Roughness'])

            # C. Tame Blown-Out White Emissive Materials to Warm 3500K
            elif node.type == 'EMISSION':
                if node.inputs['Strength'].default_value > 6.0:
                    node.inputs['Strength'].default_value = 4.0
                node.inputs['Color'].default_value = (1.0, 0.95, 0.88, 1.0)

    # =========================================================================
    # 3. LIGHT FIXER (Eliminate Specular Blobs & Enforce Architectural Spread)
    # =========================================================================
    for obj in bpy.data.objects:
        if obj.type == 'LIGHT':
            obj.visible_camera = False
            obj.visible_glossy = False
            if obj.data.type == 'AREA':
                obj.data.spread = math.radians(95)

    # =========================================================================
    # 4. OPTICAL COMPOSITOR PIPELINE (Fog Glow Bloom + Chromatic Dispersion)
    # =========================================================================
    scene.use_nodes = True
    c_tree = scene.node_tree
    c_nodes = c_tree.nodes
    c_links = c_tree.links
    c_nodes.clear()

    r_layers = c_nodes.new('CompositorNodeRLayers')
    r_layers.location = (-400, 0)

    glare = c_nodes.new('CompositorNodeGlare')
    glare.glare_type = 'FOG_GLOW'
    glare.quality = 'HIGH'
    glare.threshold = 0.85
    glare.size = 7
    glare.location = (0, 0)

    lens = c_nodes.new('CompositorNodeLensdist')
    lens.use_fit = True
    lens.inputs['Distort'].default_value = -0.008
    lens.inputs['Dispersion'].default_value = 0.0035
    lens.location = (250, 0)

    comp = c_nodes.new('CompositorNodeComposite')
    comp.location = (500, 0)

    c_links.new(r_layers.outputs['Image'], glare.inputs['Image'])
    c_links.new(glare.outputs['Image'], lens.inputs['Image'])
    c_links.new(lens.outputs['Image'], comp.inputs['Image'])

    print("✅ Universal VDC Upgrades Applied: Cycles, AgX, Micro-Bevels, Light Fixes & Compositor Active.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    apply_universal_vdc_upgrades()
```

## 6. Script 3: `03_cinematic_rigs.py` (Modular Camera, X-Ray Section & Lighting Generators)

Import or invoke these reusable functions to build multi-camera cuts, glowing Boolean architectural cross-sections, and Golden-Hour "Release" lighting rigs at any coordinate in the project.

```python
import bpy
import math

# =============================================================================
# MODULE A: CREATE ARCHITECTURAL TILT-SHIFT CAMERA SHOT
# =============================================================================
def create_archviz_shot(name, frame_start, frame_end, start_loc, end_loc, yaw_deg, lens_mm=28.0, shift_y=0.0, dof_dist=0.0):
    """
    Creates a level 2-point perspective camera with LINEAR Steadicam motion
    and binds it to a timeline marker at frame_start.
    """
    scene = bpy.context.scene
    cam_col = bpy.data.collections.get("Archviz_Cameras")
    if not cam_col:
        cam_col = bpy.data.collections.new("Archviz_Cameras")
        scene.collection.children.link(cam_col)

    cam_data = bpy.data.cameras.new(name)
    cam_data.lens = lens_mm
    cam_data.sensor_width = 36.0
    cam_data.shift_y = shift_y
    cam_data.passepartout_alpha = 0.95
    cam_data.show_composition_thirds = True
    cam_data.show_composition_center = True

    if dof_dist > 0.0:
        cam_data.dof.use_dof = True
        cam_data.dof.focus_distance = dof_dist
        cam_data.dof.aperture_fstop = 4.0

    cam_obj = bpy.data.objects.new(name, cam_data)
    cam_col.objects.link(cam_obj)

    # Lock X=90°, Y=0° so vertical lines never converge
    cam_obj.rotation_euler = (math.radians(90), 0.0, math.radians(yaw_deg))

    cam_obj.location = start_loc
    cam_obj.keyframe_insert(data_path="location", frame=frame_start)
    cam_obj.location = end_loc
    cam_obj.keyframe_insert(data_path="location", frame=frame_end)

    if cam_obj.animation_data and cam_obj.animation_data.action:
        for fcurve in cam_obj.animation_data.action.fcurves:
            for kf in fcurve.keyframe_points:
                kf.interpolation = 'LINEAR'

    marker = scene.timeline_markers.new(name=name, frame=frame_start)
    marker.camera = cam_obj
    return cam_obj


# =============================================================================
# MODULE B: ANIMATED BOOLEAN X-RAY SECTION RIG
# =============================================================================
def create_boolean_section_rig(target_objects, location, dimensions, frame_in, frame_hold_start, frame_hold_end, frame_out):
    """
    Creates an invisible animated Boolean cutter box that slices open a list of
    target architectural meshes and applies a glowing gold emissive shader ONLY
    to the sliced cross-section faces.
    """
    cut_mat = bpy.data.materials.get("MAT_VDC_Section_Glow") or bpy.data.materials.new("MAT_VDC_Section_Glow")
    cut_mat.use_nodes = True
    nodes = cut_mat.node_tree.nodes
    nodes.clear()
    
    emiss = nodes.new('ShaderNodeEmission')
    emiss.inputs['Color'].default_value = (1.0, 0.78, 0.45, 1.0) # Architectural gold
    emiss.inputs['Strength'].default_value = 6.0
    out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial')
    cut_mat.node_tree.links.new(emiss.outputs['Emission'], out.inputs['Surface'])

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.0, location=location)
    cutter = bpy.context.active_object
    cutter.name = "VDC_Boolean_Section_Cutter"
    cutter.display_type = 'WIRE'
    cutter.visible_camera = False
    cutter.visible_diffuse = False
    cutter.visible_glossy = False
    cutter.visible_shadow = False
    cutter.data.materials.append(cut_mat)

    cutter.scale = (0.001, 0.001, 0.001)
    cutter.keyframe_insert(data_path="scale", frame=frame_in)

    cutter.scale = dimensions
    cutter.keyframe_insert(data_path="scale", frame=frame_hold_start)
    cutter.keyframe_insert(data_path="scale", frame=frame_hold_end)

    cutter.scale = (0.001, 0.001, 0.001)
    cutter.keyframe_insert(data_path="scale", frame=frame_out)

    for obj in target_objects:
        if obj.type == 'MESH' and obj != cutter:
            if cut_mat.name not in obj.data.materials:
                obj.data.materials.append(cut_mat)
            mod = obj.modifiers.new(name="VDC_Section_Cut", type='BOOLEAN')
            mod.operation = 'DIFFERENCE'
            mod.object = cutter
            mod.solver = 'EXACT'

    return cutter


# =============================================================================
# MODULE C: NATURAL LIGHT "RELEASE" PORTAL & SUN RIG
# =============================================================================
def create_golden_hour_window_rig(window_location, window_yaw_deg, width=6.0, height=3.0, sun_elevation_deg=10.0):
    """
    Places a Cycles Sky Portal directly over an exterior window opening alongside
    a low-angle 2800K Golden Hour Sun to create dramatic interior light shafts.
    """
    scene = bpy.context.scene

    # 1. Cycles Interior Sky Portal (Cuts interior GI noise by 50%+)
    portal_data = bpy.data.lights.new(name="VDC_Window_Portal", type='AREA')
    portal_data.shape = 'RECTANGLE'
    portal_data.size = width
    portal_data.size_y = height
    portal_data.is_portal = True

    portal_obj = bpy.data.objects.new("VDC_Window_Portal", portal_data)
    scene.collection.objects.link(portal_obj)
    portal_obj.location = window_location
    portal_obj.rotation_euler = (math.radians(90), 0.0, math.radians(window_yaw_deg))

    # 2. Warm 2800K Directional Sunset Light
    sun_data = bpy.data.lights.new(name="VDC_Golden_Sun", type='SUN')
    sun_data.energy = 4.5
    sun_data.color = (1.0, 0.74, 0.48)
    sun_data.angle = math.radians(2.5)

    sun_obj = bpy.data.objects.new("VDC_Golden_Sun", sun_data)
    scene.collection.objects.link(sun_obj)
    sun_obj.location = window_location
    sun_obj.rotation_euler = (math.radians(90.0 - sun_elevation_deg), 0.0, math.radians(window_yaw_deg + 15.0))

    return portal_obj, sun_obj
```

## 7. Quality Assurance Verification Checklist (Pre-Render Sign-off)

Before submitting final frames or animations, the agent must verify:
- [ ] **No Vertical Convergence:** Every active camera has `rotation_euler.x == 90°` and `rotation_euler.y == 0°`.

                min_co.y = min(min_co.y, world_co.y)

    scene.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
    scene.cycles.device = 'GPU'
    scene.render.resolution_x = 3840
    scene.render.resolution_y = 2160
    scene.render.resolution_percentage = 50  # 1080p fast preview; set 100 for final 4K

    # Sampling & Albedo/Normal-Preserving Denoiser
    scene.cycles.samples = 512
    scene.cycles.adaptive_threshold = 0.015
    scene.cycles.use_denoising = True
    scene.cycles.denoiser = 'OPENIMAGEDENOISE'
    scene.cycles.denoising_input_passes = 'RGB_ALBEDO_NORMAL'

    # Architectural Light Bounce Profile
    scene.cycles.max_bounces = 12
    scene.cycles.diffuse_bounces = 4
    scene.cycles.glossy_bounces = 4
    scene.cycles.transmission_bounces = 8
    scene.cycles.volume_bounces = 2
    scene.cycles.sample_clamp_indirect = 10.0

    # AgX High-Dynamic-Range View Transform
    try:
        scene.view_settings.view_transform = 'AgX'
        scene.view_settings.look = 'AgX - Medium High Contrast'
    except TypeError:
        scene.view_settings.view_transform = 'Filmic'
        scene.view_settings.look = 'Medium High Contrast'

    # =========================================================================
    # 2. GLOBAL PBR SHADER UPGRADER (Micro-Bevels + Roughness Breakup + Emissives)
    # =========================================================================
    for mat in bpy.data.materials:
        if not mat.use_nodes or not mat.node_tree:
            continue
        nodes = mat.node_tree.nodes
        links = mat.node_tree.links

        for node in list(nodes):
            if node.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED':
                # A. Inject 3mm Architectural Micro-Bevel into unlinked Normals
                if not node.inputs['Normal'].is_linked:
                    bevel = nodes.new(type='ShaderNodeBevel')
                    bevel.samples = 4
                    bevel.inputs['Radius'].default_value = 0.003
                    bevel.location = (node.location.x - 280, node.location.y - 320)
                    links.new(bevel.outputs['Normal'], node.inputs['Normal'])

                # B. Replace flat CG Roughness with subtle procedural micro-variation
                if not node.inputs['Roughness'].is_linked:
                    base_r = node.inputs['Roughness'].default_value
                    # Clamp unrealistic 1.0 chalky surfaces
                    if base_r > 0.85:
                        base_r = 0.60
                    
                    tex_coord = nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord')
                    tex_coord.location = (node.location.x - 700, node.location.y - 100)
                    
                    noise = nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexNoise')
                    noise.inputs['Scale'].default_value = 120.0
                    noise.inputs['Detail'].default_value = 8.0
                    noise.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = 0.6
                    noise.location = (node.location.x - 500, node.location.y - 100)
                    
                    ramp = nodes.new('ShaderNodeMapRange')
                    ramp.inputs['To Min'].default_value = max(0.05, base_r - 0.06)
                    ramp.inputs['To Max'].default_value = min(0.95, base_r + 0.06)
                    ramp.location = (node.location.x - 280, node.location.y - 100)
                    
                    links.new(tex_coord.outputs['Object'], noise.inputs['Vector'])
                    links.new(noise.outputs['Fac'], ramp.inputs['Value'])
                    links.new(ramp.outputs['Result'], node.inputs['Roughness'])

            # C. Tame Blown-Out White Emissive Materials to Warm 3500K
            elif node.type == 'EMISSION':
                if node.inputs['Strength'].default_value > 6.0:
                    node.inputs['Strength'].default_value = 4.0
                node.inputs['Color'].default_value = (1.0, 0.95, 0.88, 1.0)

    # =========================================================================
    # 3. LIGHT FIXER (Eliminate Specular Blobs & Enforce Architectural Spread)
    # =========================================================================
    for obj in bpy.data.objects:
        if obj.type == 'LIGHT':
            obj.visible_camera = False
            obj.visible_glossy = False
            if obj.data.type == 'AREA':
                obj.data.spread = math.radians(95)

    # =========================================================================
    # 4. OPTICAL COMPOSITOR PIPELINE (Fog Glow Bloom + Chromatic Dispersion)
    # =========================================================================
    scene.use_nodes = True
    c_tree = scene.node_tree
    c_nodes = c_tree.nodes
    c_links = c_tree.links
    c_nodes.clear()

    r_layers = c_nodes.new('CompositorNodeRLayers')
    r_layers.location = (-400, 0)

    glare = c_nodes.new('CompositorNodeGlare')
    glare.glare_type = 'FOG_GLOW'
    glare.quality = 'HIGH'
    glare.threshold = 0.85
    glare.size = 7
    glare.location = (0, 0)

    lens = c_nodes.new('CompositorNodeLensdist')
    lens.use_fit = True
    lens.inputs['Distort'].default_value = -0.008
    lens.inputs['Dispersion'].default_value = 0.0035
    lens.location = (250, 0)

    comp = c_nodes.new('CompositorNodeComposite')
    comp.location = (500, 0)

    c_links.new(r_layers.outputs['Image'], glare.inputs['Image'])
    c_links.new(glare.outputs['Image'], lens.inputs['Image'])
    c_links.new(lens.outputs['Image'], comp.inputs['Image'])

    print("✅ Universal VDC Upgrades Applied: Cycles, AgX, Micro-Bevels, Light Fixes & Compositor Active.")

if __name__ == "__main__":

import bpy
import math

# =============================================================================
# MODULE A: CREATE ARCHITECTURAL TILT-SHIFT CAMERA SHOT
# =============================================================================
def create_archviz_shot(name, frame_start, frame_end, start_loc, end_loc, yaw_deg, lens_mm=28.0, shift_y=0.0, dof_dist=0.0):
    """
    Creates a level 2-point perspective camera with LINEAR Steadicam motion
    and binds it to a timeline marker at frame_start.
    """
    scene = bpy.context.scene
    cam_col = bpy.data.collections.get("Archviz_Cameras")
    if not cam_col:
        cam_col = bpy.data.collections.new("Archviz_Cameras")
        scene.collection.children.link(cam_col)

    cam_data = bpy.data.cameras.new(name)
    cam_data.lens = lens_mm
    cam_data.sensor_width = 36.0
    cam_data.shift_y = shift_y
    cam_data.passepartout_alpha = 0.95
    cam_data.show_composition_thirds = True
    cam_data.show_composition_center = True

    if dof_dist > 0.0:
        cam_data.dof.use_dof = True
        cam_data.dof.focus_distance = dof_dist
        cam_data.dof.aperture_fstop = 4.0

    cam_obj = bpy.data.objects.new(name, cam_data)
    cam_col.objects.link(cam_obj)

    # Lock X=90°, Y=0° so vertical lines never converge
    cam_obj.rotation_euler = (math.radians(90), 0.0, math.radians(yaw_deg))

    cam_obj.location = start_loc
    cam_obj.keyframe_insert(data_path="location", frame=frame_start)
    cam_obj.location = end_loc
    cam_obj.keyframe_insert(data_path="location", frame=frame_end)

    if cam_obj.animation_data and cam_obj.animation_data.action:
        for fcurve in cam_obj.animation_data.action.fcurves:
            for kf in fcurve.keyframe_points:
                kf.interpolation = 'LINEAR'

    marker = scene.timeline_markers.new(name=name, frame=frame_start)
    marker.camera = cam_obj
    return cam_obj


# =============================================================================
# MODULE B: ANIMATED BOOLEAN X-RAY SECTION RIG
# =============================================================================
def create_boolean_section_rig(target_objects, location, dimensions, frame_in, frame_hold_start, frame_hold_end, frame_out):
    """
    Creates an invisible animated Boolean cutter box that slices open a list of
    target architectural meshes and applies a glowing gold emissive shader ONLY
    to the sliced cross-section faces.
    """
    cut_mat = bpy.data.materials.get("MAT_VDC_Section_Glow") or bpy.data.materials.new("MAT_VDC_Section_Glow")
    cut_mat.use_nodes = True
    nodes = cut_mat.node_tree.nodes
    nodes.clear()
    
    emiss = nodes.new('ShaderNodeEmission')
    emiss.inputs['Color'].default_value = (1.0, 0.78, 0.45, 1.0) # Architectural gold
    emiss.inputs['Strength'].default_value = 6.0
    out = nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputMaterial')
    cut_mat.node_tree.links.new(emiss.outputs['Emission'], out.inputs['Surface'])

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.0, location=location)
    cutter = bpy.context.active_object
    cutter.name = "VDC_Boolean_Section_Cutter"
    cutter.display_type = 'WIRE'
    cutter.visible_camera = False
    cutter.visible_diffuse = False
    cutter.visible_glossy = False
    cutter.visible_shadow = False
    cutter.data.materials.append(cut_mat)

    cutter.scale = (0.001, 0.001, 0.001)
    cutter.keyframe_insert(data_path="scale", frame=frame_in)

    cutter.scale = dimensions
    cutter.keyframe_insert(data_path="scale", frame=frame_hold_start)
    cutter.keyframe_insert(data_path="scale", frame=frame_hold_end)

    cutter.scale = (0.001, 0.001, 0.001)
    cutter.keyframe_insert(data_path="scale", frame=frame_out)

    for obj in target_objects:
        if obj.type == 'MESH' and obj != cutter:
            if cut_mat.name not in obj.data.materials:
                obj.data.materials.append(cut_mat)
            mod = obj.modifiers.new(name="VDC_Section_Cut", type='BOOLEAN')
            mod.operation = 'DIFFERENCE'
            mod.object = cutter
            mod.solver = 'EXACT'

    return cutter


# =============================================================================
# MODULE C: NATURAL LIGHT "RELEASE" PORTAL & SUN RIG
# =============================================================================
def create_golden_hour_window_rig(window_location, window_yaw_deg, width=6.0, height=3.0, sun_elevation_deg=10.0):
    """
    Places a Cycles Sky Portal directly over an exterior window opening alongside
    a low-angle 2800K Golden Hour Sun to create dramatic interior light shafts.
    """
    scene = bpy.context.scene

    # 1. Cycles Interior Sky Portal (Cuts interior GI noise by 50%+)
    portal_data = bpy.data.lights.new(name="VDC_Window_Portal", type='AREA')
    portal_data.shape = 'RECTANGLE'
    portal_data.size = width
    portal_data.size_y = height
    portal_data.is_portal = True

    portal_obj = bpy.data.objects.new("VDC_Window_Portal", portal_data)
    scene.collection.objects.link(portal_obj)
    portal_obj.location = window_location
    portal_obj.rotation_euler = (math.radians(90), 0.0, math.radians(window_yaw_deg))

    # 2. Warm 2800K Directional Sunset Light
    sun_data = bpy.data.lights.new(name="VDC_Golden_Sun", type='SUN')
    sun_data.energy = 4.5
    sun_data.color = (1.0, 0.74, 0.48)
    sun_data.angle = math.radians(2.5)

    sun_obj = bpy.data.objects.new("VDC_Golden_Sun", sun_data)
    scene.collection.objects.link(sun_obj)
    sun_obj.location = window_location
    sun_obj.rotation_euler = (math.radians(90.0 - sun_elevation_deg), 0.0, math.radians(window_yaw_deg + 15.0))

    return portal_obj, sun_obj

## 8. Agency-grade additions (repo maintainers, 2026-11-06)

What separates a $100k agency film from a good render is mostly decided before Cycles runs: the brief, the boards,
the edit and the sound. Then comes discipline about light and material values, and a QC pass nobody skips. Every
API named below was checked against bpy 5.0.1 on 2026-11-06.

### 8.1 Pre-production (decide the film before building it)

- **Brief in one sentence:** who watches it (owner, board, residents, jury), what they must believe at the end,
  and the runtime. 45–90 s is the usual length for an owner or marketing film; residents need 20–40 s per notice.
- **Reference board:** 6–10 frames from real architectural photography and agency films, one per shot, noting
  lens, camera height, time of day and light direction. Match a mood, never copy a frame.
- **Shot list as data:** one JSON entry per shot with lens, shift, keys, focus and an exposure trim, like
  `cinema.shots.json`. Code reads it, so changing the edit doesn't mean editing code.
- **Animatic first:** 10–25% resolution, 4–8 samples, Cycles. Workbench and EEVEE render blank frames headless, so
  Cycles is the only option here. Cut it to the music before spending any real render time. Agencies lock the
  edit at animatic stage; re-cutting after final renders is the most expensive mistake.
- **Cut to music:** shot lengths in whole beats (e.g. 80 BPM: 3 s = 4 beats), with chord changes on the cuts.
  `cinema_score.py` shows how.
- **Handles:** render 8–12 extra frames at both ends of every shot so the edit can slip without re-rendering.

### 8.2 VDC/BIM import hygiene (fix the model before lighting it)

- **Recenter near the origin.** BIM exports often sit at state-plane or survey coordinates, hundreds of km from 0.
  Float precision then makes animated cameras jitter and causes shadow and z-fighting artifacts. Move the model so
  the area of interest is within about 1 km of the origin, and record the offset as a custom property so it can be
  undone.
- **Apply scale and rotation** (`transform_apply(location=False, rotation=True, scale=True)`), recalculate normals,
  and merge by distance at 0.1 mm.
- **Find and fix coplanar duplicates.** Hunt for z-fighting with a diagnostic frame at grazing angles: overlapping
  slabs and finishes, a wall drawn twice by two trades. Delete the duplicate or offset it by 1 mm, and record which
  one stays (the governing trade).
- **Keep identity.** Carry the IFC GlobalId or Revit element ID into `cie_id` and other custom properties, so a
  frame can be traced back to the element that drew it. Import IFC with `ifcopenshell` (not installed;
  `uv add ifcopenshell` and check `uv lock` keeps numpy<2 for bpy) or the Bonsai extension. Speckle is an option
  for live Revit to Blender.
- **Bevel what the camera sees.** The Bevel shader in the directive is costly per sample and doesn't change
  silhouettes. For hero objects in close-up shots, a Bevel modifier (2–3 mm, `harden_normals`) plus a
  WeightedNormal modifier looks better and renders faster. Use it only in the presentation scene, never in a spec
  build.

### 8.3 Cameras and motion

- **Heights:** interiors at 1.2–1.5 m (just below eye level reads as more generous). Exteriors at 1.6 m for
  pedestrian views, or 4–15 m for a modest elevated view. Drone-height views are for context only.
- **Speeds:** a dolly or slider moves at 0.2–0.6 m/s. Any faster reads as a video game. Pans are rare and slow
  (under 5°/s).
- **Detail inserts:** 50–85 mm, still level (Rule 1), shallow depth of field (f/2–f/4) on materials and
  hardware. One insert every 3–4 shots gives the edit rhythm. The house film's walnut slat insert is an example.
  Wider shots stay at f/5.6–f/11 so the architecture stays sharp.
- **Bokeh:** set `dof.aperture_blades` to 7–9 and a small `aperture_rotation`; round bokeh from blades = 0 reads
  as CG.
- **Motion blur on:** `render.use_motion_blur = True`, `motion_blur_shutter = 0.5` (180°). Without it, linear camera
  moves strobe.
- **Handheld life (optional):** an `FModifierNoise` on the location f-curves only (0.5–2 mm amplitude, slow).
  Never put it on rotation, because Rule 1 locks the camera level.
- **Aspect ratio:** 16:9 per the directive. For marketing films, 2.39:1 is a valid option
  (the house film uses it); render 16:9 and crop, or set the resolution directly.

### 8.4 Light (get the values physical, then make it beautiful)

- **Sky:** `ShaderNodeTexSky` with `sky_type = 'MULTIPLE_SCATTERING'` for physically based daylight. Or an HDRI
  from Poly Haven (`bmodels.polyhaven`, checksum-locked, CC0) when real cloud and context reflections matter. Rotate
  the sun to the site's true north and a real date and time, and record both.
- **Color temperature:** set `light.use_temperature = True` and `light.temperature` in kelvin. That avoids
  hand-picked RGB: 2700–3000 K for residential, 3500 K for corridors (the directive's compression phase), 4000 K
  for back-of-house. Use `ShaderNodeBlackbody` for emissive fixtures, so a fixture's glow matches its light.
- **Real fixtures:** when the fixture schedule names a product, drive the area or spot light with that
  manufacturer's IES file (`ShaderNodeTexIES`). Wall-washer scallops are what make a corridor look real.
- **Exposure, not wattage:** balance a shot with `view_settings.exposure` (per shot, from the shot list's exposure
  trim) and `light.exposure`. Don't scale every light up.
- **Light linking:** `obj.light_linking.receiver_collection` / `blocker_collection` (Cycles) for a rim on one
  object or a kicker on the hero material without spilling everywhere. Use it sparingly and only in presentation
  scenes.
- **Light groups:** add `view_layer.lightgroups` (e.g. `sun`, `sky`, `interior`, `fixtures`) and set `obj.lightgroup`.
  The balance between day and fixtures can then be re-graded in post without re-rendering. It's the cheapest
  agency trick there is.
- **Noise control:** `cycles.use_light_tree` (on by default) for many fixtures. `cycles.use_guiding = True` (path
  guiding, CPU only) helps interiors lit through windows. `blur_glossy` at 0.5–1.0, caustics off
  (`caustics_reflective`/`caustics_refractive = False`) unless they're the subject.
- **Color views:** AgX "AgX - Medium High Contrast" is the default and verified. "AgX - Punchy" works for exterior
  dusk. "ACES 2.0" and "Khronos PBR Neutral" also exist in this build. Pick one per film and never mix them. Note
  that in 5.0.1 the look names carry the "AgX - " prefix.

### 8.5 Materials, scale and dressing

- **Albedo discipline:** the brightest real paint is about 0.8–0.85 linear albedo, so never use 1.0 white. Black
  materials stay at 0.02–0.04 or above. Concrete sits around 0.3–0.4 and wood around 0.2–0.45. Most "CG look"
  comes from albedos that are too bright or too saturated.
- **Real-world mapping:** for BIM without UVs, use box projection (`ShaderNodeTexImage.projection = 'BOX'`,
  `projection_blend` 0.1–0.2) in object or world space, in metres. `bmodels.polyhaven` already does this.
  Diagnostic check: a brick course is 75 mm with a 10 mm joint (UK/metric) or 2⅝" per course (US modular), and
  carpet tiles are 500–610 mm.
- **Break repetition:** use `ShaderNodeObjectInfo` → Random to vary hue, value and roughness by ±2–5% per object
  (doors, tiles, planks). Rotate and offset texture coordinates per object too.
- **Wear where it would really occur:** use `ShaderNodeAmbientOcclusion` or Pointiness (Cycles) for faint grime in
  corners and wear on edges. Keep it under 5% in a new building. "New construction" should look new, not dirty.
- **Glass:** model glazing with real thickness, IOR 1.5 and a faint green-blue tint. Use portals at window
  openings (the directive's Module C) instead of hiding glass from shadow rays, which leaks light.
- **People and life:** a few scaled, animated 3D people (licensed, e.g. Renderpeople or AXYZ anima), sitting or
  walking slowly, motion-blurred. Never more than the space would really hold. In occupied-building films, people
  must not suggest residents in unsafe positions near work zones.
- **Vegetation:** scatter with Geometry Nodes using Poly Haven or licensed plant assets, with density and scale
  variation (±15%), and wind as a slow noise on a GN rotation. See the `scenario-blender-geometry-nodes` skill.
- **Licensing:** record every downloaded asset's source, license and checksum (`bmodels.polyhaven` writes the lock
  for Poly Haven). Prefer CC0 (Poly Haven, ambientCG). Megascans/Fab and paid people libraries have
  per-project terms, so check them before they appear in a client deliverable.

### 8.6 Rendering pipeline

- **Profiles:** at least three (animatic, preview, final), like `PROFILES` in `cinema.py`. Benchmark one frame per
  shot before launching a sequence, and estimate total hours. `cinema.py --bench` is the example.
- **Final quality:** noise threshold 0.005–0.01 with enough max samples that the denoiser does little work. An
  over-denoised animation smears and flickers frame to frame. Keep `use_animated_seed = False` for stills; for
  animation, test both on a 2 s clip and look at the flicker.
- **`render.use_persistent_data = True`** for sequences (it keeps the BVH and textures between frames).
- **Render to EXR, grade later:** multilayer EXR, half float, `DWAA` or `ZIP` codec, with Denoising Data
  (`view_layer.cycles.denoising_store_passes`), light groups, Cryptomatte object and material
  (`use_pass_cryptomatte_*`) and Mist. Grade and comp from those. Never bake a look into 8-bit PNGs you can't
  re-grade.
- **Parallel GPUs:** one frame per worker with a claim file, like `claim_frames`/`check_claim` in `cinema.py`. The
  same Blender (5.0.1) and the same `uv.lock` on every worker, with the source scene hash recorded per frame.
- **Committed scenes stay self-contained:** pack textures, HDRIs and sounds before saving (`bm audit-blends`).

### 8.7 Post, sound and delivery

- **Grade:** a light touch. Slight lift in the shadows, protected highlights, a gentle vignette, and 1–2% film
  grain (it hides banding in skies and walls). Grade in Blender's compositor (5.0 node-group API) or in
  DaVinci Resolve (free) from the EXRs. The repo's `vision` group (OpenCV 4.10, numpy<2) handles scripted
  finishing, see `cinema_finish.py`.
- **Sound is half the film:** a score cut to the edit, room tone in every interior, and quiet foley for doors,
  footsteps, the elevator and the city. Agencies spend real money here. The repo has the `audio` group
  (`uv sync --group audio`: Piper TTS narration, SciPy) and `cinema_score.py` for an original score. Licensed music
  needs its license recorded with the deliverable.
- **Typography:** one typeface, generous tracking, a title and an end card, sparing lower-thirds. On every frame,
  the "illustrative, not a contract document" strip sits below the image, never over it.
- **Masters:** ProRes 422 HQ (FFmpeg codec `PRORES`) or DNxHR as the master. H.264 or H.265 at high bitrate (4K: about
  40–60 Mb/s) for review and web, plus a 1080p version for email and phones. Use Rec.709 or sRGB for every
  deliverable unless an HDR deliverable is explicitly ordered (`Rec.2100-PQ` exists in this build but needs an HDR
  grade). Files over 1 MB go to GitHub Releases (`bm publish`).

### 8.8 QC: automate the boring checks, look at everything else

On top of section 0 and section 7, run these on every rendered sequence, all from the repo with numpy/OpenCV:
- **Blank or black frames:** mean and std per frame, like the builder's `image_is_blank`.
- **Clipping:** the share of pixels at the top or bottom of the range per frame. Flag over 0.5% outside fixtures and
  windows.
- **Flicker:** the frame-to-frame change in mean luminance within a shot, and in a 64-px grid. A spike that isn't a
  cut is denoiser flicker or a missing frame.
- **Frame count and continuity:** every frame in every shot is present and in order, with the same resolution and
  source hash (no frame from an old scene version).
- **Then watch it** at full size, at real speed, with sound, on a reasonably calibrated display and on a phone.
  Write down which version you watched.

### 8.9 What makes a VDC film worth more than a beautiful one

Agencies sell beauty. This repo sells beauty that is true, and that is the premium:
- **Truth layer:** every film has a matching provenance pass (the review colors) of its key frames. Every visible
  assumed element is known, and it is listed in the deliverable README.
- **Construction storytelling:** use 4D sequences tied to the schedule (`cie` activities), existing and proposed
  as separate scenes cut together, X-ray and section reveals of concealed conditions (Module B, gold cut faces),
  exploded axonometrics for trade sequence, and animated callouts that cite the drawing (sheet and detail) next to
  the thing they label.
- **Occupied buildings:** show protection, egress and the work zone as their own collection; residents should
  be able to read "where, when, how long" in one shot.
- **Never fake it to make it pretty.** No moved walls for a better composition, no invented windows for light, no
  removed structure that's really there. If a shot needs it, it's a different shot.

| Tool | Use | Status here |
|---|---|---|
| `bmodels.polyhaven` + `assets/hdri` | CC0 textures, models and HDRIs, checksum-locked, box-projected | in repo |
| `vision` group (OpenCV 4.10) | finishing, QC metrics, review sheets | installed by default |
| `audio` group (Piper TTS, SciPy) | narration, generated score | `uv sync --group audio` |
| FFmpeg | encode ProRes/H.264/H.265, contact sheets | on PATH (`bm doctor`) |
| `ifcopenshell` | IFC import with GlobalIds | not installed: `uv add`, check numpy<2 |
| Bonsai (Blender extension) | IFC authoring/import inside Blender | not installed; extensions install via `bpy.ops.extensions`, verify headless first |
| Speckle connector | live Revit/Rhino → Blender | external, not set up |
| DaVinci Resolve (free) | edit, grade from EXR, ProRes masters | external app |
| Paid add-ons (e.g. Photographer, Geo-Scatter, Gaffer) | GUI conveniences for exposure, scatter and light management | optional; bake their results into the `.blend` and never make a headless step depend on them |
